objective: Coordinator's pick (18 November 2026), KNOT-CAP-20261117-001's second direction: why do presentations of the same line by betweenness knots (the line of five with its shared distinction at an end, next to an end or in the middle; the six-starts) grow different numbers of orders under the knot-local fewest-states rule KF3? Find an invariant of how the knots meet that predicts the order distribution, prove what can be proved, cover the untested next-to-end position, and say whether the six-starts' agreement through n = 9 follows from the same mechanism. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
title: Why how the knots meet changes the number of orders
